sentences.text: Learned Counsel for the Appellant submits that it is settled law that the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is a beneficial legislation and the Courts are required to be benevolent, while condoning the delay.
Reliance is placed on the judgment dated 05.11.2024 passed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court in Pravesh Sharma vs. Sumeer Mehta & Anr (HDFC ERGO General Insurance Co Ltd), in this behalf.

entities.text: Pravesh Sharma vs. Sumeer Mehta & Anr (HDFC ERGO General Insurance Co Ltd)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. The Supreme Court in the case of Sheo Raj Singh v. Union of India; (2023) 10 SCC 531 has held that the power to condone delay must be exercised based on the cause and not the length of the delay.

sentences.text: A genuine explanation and not a mere excuse is required.

8.1. A Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Savitri Devi v. Hasan Khan; 2016 SCC OnLine Del 1530 has held that the delay by itself should not defeat the interest of justice, particularly in cases of benevolent jurisdiction under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

The settled law that the insurance company must abide by its responsibility in terms of the third party insurance policy though it may claim the right to recover should have been applied by the tribunal to the case at hand.
The delay in filing appeal is condoned but with rider that insurer would not be burdened with interest for the period of delay."
